comment: Seccomp profile for the rootless BuildKit daemon (pfa-system/buildkitd).
Rootless BuildKit on this Fedora/k3s host cannot run with the default
profile: the process sandbox cannot mount /proc, so the daemon is started
with --oci-worker-no-process-sandbox (k8s/system/buildkit.yaml). That flag
puts a build step in the daemon's own namespaces, where it can signal the
daemon, read another process's files through /proc/<pid>/root, and inspect
process memory. The pod used to run with seccompProfile: Unconfined, which
left all of that reachable.
This is a deny-list, not an allow-list: the rootless runtime needs a wide
set of syscalls and an allow-list is where builds break. It blocks the
syscalls that turn 'a build step' into 'control of the build daemon' or
'a kernel exploit': cross-process memory access, tracing, eBPF, perf,
io_uring, userfaultfd, module loading and kexec.
The keyring syscalls (keyctl, add_key, request_key) are deliberately NOT
denied: runc joins a session keyring while initialising every container,
so denying them makes every RUN fail with 'unable to join session keyring'.
Install on the node (the kubelet resolves Localhost profiles relative to
its seccomp root):
sudo install -D -m 0644 k8s/system/seccomp/buildkitd.json \
/var/lib/kubelet/seccomp/profiles/buildkitd.json
Then roll the daemon. Test a build with a real RUN step: this file must
not block anything rootlesskit, runc or the build itself needs.
